fields.description: Migrate Endless to an event-sourced architecture with per-project event logs and SQLite as a rebuildable projection, in stages.
fields.analysis:
# Where the rebuild work moved (2026-08-25)

This epic held the April five-stage design. The rebuild-reliability half of it
is owned by **E-1935**, filed in August for exactly that, and the measured state
of `rebuild-db --confirm` — the full transitive FK closure, the four gaps and
their owners, and the ordering constraint on `sessions.task_id` — lives in
E-1935's analysis rather than being duplicated here.

E-1041, E-2062 and E-1728 moved to E-1935 with it. E-894 and its subtree moved
to E-1486, the port epic, being port work rather than event-sourcing work.

What remains here is the design-stage work: E-806, E-809, E-810, E-813, E-814,
E-816, E-817, plus E-910 and E-914.

## From the description

Per-project .endless/events.jsonl + global changelog repo, with SQLite as rebuildable projection. 5-stage migration.

fields.description: Generate Markdown files on disk from ledger content, and keep them in sync, when an external tool Endless works alongside requires them.
fields.notes:
Parked.

Revive against a concrete external tool, which will specify the requirement better than this placeholder.

fields.description: Implement a Go package that serializes hybrid logical clock timestamps as strings that sort lexicographically and stay human-readable.
fields.analysis:
Go package at internal/kairos/.

Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.SSSSSS-XXXX-NNN. Node ID per-installation stored in ~/.config/endless/node_id. Build inside Endless, extract as standalone package later.

fields.description: Define the fixed event envelope and the initial closed set of task, dependency, session, and project event kinds, stored in per-machine segment files.
fields.analysis:
Line-delimited JSON. Initial task/dep/session/project event kinds including revisit status and tags. Events stored in segmented files per node: .endless/events/events-{node_id}-{seq}.jsonl.

Each machine writes only to its own segments; git merge adds files, never line conflicts.

fields.description: Implement Go subcommands that append events to per-machine segment files, with the Python CLI calling them while the database stays authoritative.
fields.analysis:
Python CLI shells out to Go for all event writes — single implementation, no format divergence. Writes to .endless/events/events-{node_id}-{seq}.jsonl. Rotation when segment exceeds threshold.

DB remains authoritative in Stage 1.

Enables sqlc from day one.

fields.description: Make the user config directory optionally a git repo holding cross-project events, synced across machines with git pull and push.
fields.analysis:
No separate changelog repo.

Cross-project events (project registered, cross-project deps) go here. .gitignore excludes endless.db (rebuildable projection) and local cache files. Multi-machine sync via git pull/push in this directory.

fields.description: Build a deterministic projection engine and a rebuild command that recreate the SQLite database from event logs, validated against the current database.
fields.analysis:
Given same events, any machine produces same DB state.

Implement endless rebuild-db.

Validate projection matches current DB.

fields.title: Make event logs authoritative over SQLite
fields.description: Make event logs authoritative: every write goes through the Go event writer first, and SQLite becomes a cache updated by projection.
fields.analysis: Projection updates SQLite incrementally as side effect. Python CLI is fully dependent on Go for writes. DB becomes a cache. endless rebuild-db supported for disaster recovery.

fields.description: Implement a compact command that merges old event segments into a local, uncommitted state file for faster replay.
fields.analysis:
Local-only operation, not committed to git.

Never modifies git-committed segment files. Old segments optionally prunable after checkpoint, but that's a future optimization.

fields.description: Migrate task ordering from integer sort order to lexicographic rank strings, so a task can be inserted between two others without renumbering.
fields.analysis:
Use morikuni/go-lexorank.

Insertion between two tasks without renumbering.

Background rebalance pass.

fields.description: Refactor the catch-all task text field into separate plan, acceptance, design, and notes fields, moving existing text into plan.
fields.analysis: Each gets own event kind. Migration: existing text → plan field, others empty.

fields.description: Implement a task dependency model with blocks, parent-child and related types, including cross-project dependencies, and use its graph when task next picks work.
fields.analysis: dep.created/dep.removed events. Cross-project deps via global ID. Dependency graph in projection. endless task next uses graph + tier + phase + status.

fields.analysis: Gates block close with clear error.

fields.title: Handle multi-agent write conflicts

fields.notes: Consolidates E-815.

fields.description: Implement a workflow that parks invariant violations as conflict records, surfaces them in the dashboard, CLI and MCP, and resolves each with a new event.

Mike constantly has to remind Claude to record tasks, decisions, and justifications.

fields.description: Hide the child status summary in the needs-attention section's compact rows, since it counted all active children rather than only those needing attention.

a dedicated 'decision' item type?

Sibling to E-852 (which shipped narrow blocks/blocked-by support). Broader scope: make all task_deps relations first-class via CLI rather than requiring manual SQL or text references in descriptions. Punch list (vocabulary decision in E-958, blocking implementation):

Schema accepts any dep_type string (CHECK constraints removed), so no migration needed. Implementation order: settle vocabulary first (blocked on E-958), then ship at-creation flags + show-all-relations together (highest impact), then primitive + reverse lookups.

fields.title: Add per-session git worktrees and a topic-drift gate
fields.description: Add git worktrees per session and per task, with single ownership and a clean main to land into, plus a gate that catches topic drift between sessions.

Pre-epic-era umbrella: E-968 workstream 3 with 14+ children that land individually; epics did not exist when filed (2026-04). Retyped per review.

## From the description

Workstream 3 of E-968.

Blocked by E-969 (plan-bearing detection), E-970 (phrase storage), E-972 (project resolution).
fields.analysis:
Two flavors: per-session worktrees (auto-created on session start, removed on session end) and dedicated task worktrees (for plan-bearing tasks; persist across sessions). Rust-style ownership: at most one owner at a time, transferable via .endless/worktree.lock (atomic O_EXCL claim, stale via kill -0, released on SessionEnd). Main = sacred clean integration target; 'endless worktree land' refuses dirty main. Behavioral gate: UserPromptSubmit hook injects active-task system reminder (Layer 1) plus deterministic phrase match against E-970's pivot kind (Layer 2); PIVOT word as deliberate user override; gate clearance via task add or task start (CLI verb required, not chat ack).

fields.title: Refactor file-path CLI flags to a --xxx-file convention
fields.description: Refactor CLI flags across endless so any flag taking a file path is named --xxx-file and the bare --xxx flag takes inline content, cutting over in one step.
fields.context: Today some flags carry inline values (--description <text>) and others carry file paths despite the flag name implying inline content (--text <file>, --prompt <file>).
fields.analysis:
Today the CLI's content flags are inconsistent three different ways for the same kind of
(multi-line) content:

- `--text` takes a FILE PATH (dest `text_file`) but the name reads like inline content.
- `--analysis` takes inline content OR a path via `@file` magic (added by E-1329).
- `--outcome` / `--description` take inline content only.

This forces the user to remember which flag means which, and it has already produced a latent
bug: the research handoff template instructs `endless task update … --outcome <file>`, but
`--outcome` has no file form, so the literal path is stored as the outcome text.

## Decision (locked with Mike 2026-06-20)

- Every **long-form content flag** gets BOTH forms: bare `--xxx` carries **inline** content,
  `--xxx-file` carries a **file path**. Applies to: **text, analysis, outcome, description**.
- **justification** and **reason** stay **inline-only** (typically short) — a deliberate
  partial-consistency exception, not an oversight.
- **Remove the `@file` magic** on `--analysis` (E-1329, cli.py); `--analysis-file`
  replaces it. One mechanism, no magic. (No auto-detect of path-vs-inline — brittleness
  outweighs convenience.)
- **Hard cutover**, no alias / migration window (pre-1.0, move-fast, no-legacy).

## Consequence to watch

`--text` today IS the file-path flag, so the change INVERTS it: `--text` becomes inline and
`--text-file` becomes the path form. Every existing `--text <path>` call site (code, templates,
docs, tests) must become `--text-file <path>`.

## Coordination (not blockers)

- E-1000 (text→plan rename): whichever name survives, the `--xxx`/`--xxx-file` split applies.
- E-1554 (adds `--notes`): should follow this convention when it lands.
- Independent of the field-separation design (E-999); applies to whichever flag names survive.
- Origin: E-989 finalization.

## From the description

Apply uniformly across all endless commands.

Endless is pre-1.0 and 'move fast' applies; recommend hard cutover in one shot rather than a migration window.

fields.title: Block Claude git commits on main
fields.description: Block git commit from Claude sessions when the working directory is the main checkout, allowing worktrees and in-progress merges, and show the denial to Claude.
fields.notes: standalone follow-up to E-971, smaller scope, immediately shippable.
fields.context: Claude keeps making 'tidy-up' commits directly on main instead of in a worktree; stated discipline doesn't hold.
fields.analysis:
Mechanism enforcement for the per-session-worktree discipline. Standalone follow-up to E-971; smaller scope than the full worktree+gate work, immediately shippable.

## Why

Claude (this conversation, multiple violations on 2026-04-29) keeps making 'tidy-up' commits directly on main instead of in a worktree. Stated discipline alone doesn't hold; the easy path needs to be the right path. Mechanical guard required.

Discussed git pre-commit hooks first; rejected because:
- Per-clone install (manual; not a product feature)
- Not composable (one script per hook type per clone)
- Bash hook is Windows-hostile

Better layer: extend the Claude Code hook surface endless already owns (cmd/endless-hook/claude.go). PreToolUse fires on every Bash call; we add one rule.

## Rule

PreToolUse handler for Bash:
1. Parse the command. If not 'git commit ...', allow.
2. Resolve cwd's repo via 'git rev-parse --git-common-dir' (E-972's pattern). If cwd is in a worktree (.git is a file, not a directory), allow.
3. If cwd is main's working tree AND there's no .git/MERGE_MSG (i.e., not in the middle of a merge), deny with an actionable message:

   'Direct commits to main are not allowed. Make changes in a worktree (.endless/worktrees/<id>/) on a per-task branch, then ff-merge. See endless worktree land (E-971) when shipped.'

4. Otherwise allow.

Returns deny via Claude Code hook response; the rejection appears in Claude's context, not silently in stderr. No --no-verify equivalent in Claude Code hooks.

## Composes with E-971

The W3 design (E-971) puts the behavioral gate (UserPromptSubmit Layer 1/2) and worktree-task match check in PreToolUse. This rule is another PreToolUse check in the same 'discipline subsystem'. Could fold into E-971 but standalone is cleaner because:
- Doesn't depend on per-session worktree creation existing
- Doesn't depend on plan-bearing detection
- Just requires recognizing 'git commit' in Bash payload and checking cwd
- Can ship before E-971 lands and start enforcing immediately

## Critical files

- cmd/endless-hook/claude.go - extend handlePreToolUse with a Bash-command branch that detects git commit; helper to detect worktree-vs-main using 'git rev-parse --git-common-dir' or filepath.IsDir on cwd's .git.

## Acceptance criteria

(a) From main checkout, Claude bash 'git commit -m foo' is denied with the actionable message.
(b) From inside a worktree, 'git commit -m foo' succeeds.
(c) From main during an active merge (.git/MERGE_MSG present), 'git commit' is allowed (so 'git merge' completing a non-ff merge isn't blocked).
(d) Non-commit git commands ('git status', 'git diff', etc.) are unaffected.

## Cross-platform note

Hook binary is Go; builds for Windows/macOS/Linux. The git commands invoked ('git rev-parse --git-common-dir') are portable. No bash-specific logic.

## From the description

Layer: extend the existing Claude Code hook (cmd/endless-hook/claude.go) with a PreToolUse Bash rule that denies 'git commit' when cwd is main's working tree (allow worktrees and active merges). Returns deny via Claude Code hook response so the rejection appears in Claude's context.

Acceptance criteria in the analysis field.

fields.title: Research git hooks to block non-Claude commits on main
fields.description: Research using git hooks to block commits on main made outside Claude Code, such as direct user commits, IDE integrations, scripts and other AI agents.
fields.notes: Companion to E-1012 (Claude Code hook for blocking commits-on-main).
fields.context: E-1012 catches Claude's bash 'git commit' calls;
fields.analysis:
Companion to E-1012 (Claude Code hook for blocking commits-on-main). E-1012 catches Claude's bash invocations of 'git commit'. This task captures the deferred broader-scope option: git hooks for catching the USER's direct 'git commit' on main (or any other tool that bypasses the Claude Code hook layer).

## Why deferred

E-1012 covers the actual current problem (Claude's discipline failures). Git hooks add coverage for:
- User typing 'git commit' directly in their terminal
- Other tools (IDE git integrations, scripts, sibling AI agents not using Claude Code) committing
- CI bots running outside the Claude Code surface

These aren't current pain points. Filing now to keep the option visible; not for execution until E-1012 ships and we identify a real case the Claude Code layer doesn't catch.

## Challenges to design through (when revisited)

(1) **Distribution**. Git hooks live in .git/hooks/, NOT in the repo. Requires installation step. Endless can manage this via 'endless setup' (already installs Claude Code hooks); add an option to install/update git hooks.

(2) **Composability**. Only one script per hook type per clone. If user already has a pre-commit hook (linter, format check, conventional-commits validator, etc.), endless's hook fights it. Possible solutions:
  - Hook-runner pattern: endless's hook delegates to a chain of sub-hooks (the user's existing hook plus endless's rule). Pre-commit (the Python tool, https://pre-commit.com) does this.
  - Detect existing hook on install and prepend/append our logic.
  - Use core.hooksPath to a directory we manage; user's existing hooks moved into it.
  None are great.

(3) **Cross-platform**. Bash hooks are Windows-hostile. Options:
  - Write hooks in Go, ship as endless-hook-precommit binary, hook is a one-line wrapper invoking the binary.
  - Skip Windows; document it.
  Tmux is also non-Windows, so endless's primary surface today is Unix-y; Windows may be deferable.

(4) **Bypass**. 'git commit --no-verify' silently bypasses. Pre-commit hooks can't prevent --no-verify. Documented as a deliberate user choice; live with it.

(5) **Worktree handling**. The hook needs to detect cwd is in a worktree (allow) vs. main (deny). 'git rev-parse --git-dir' returns the absolute .git path; if it's '<repo>/.git/worktrees/<name>' it's a worktree, otherwise main. Portable.

## Likely approach (sketch, not commitment)

Endless ships a Go binary 'endless-git-precommit'. 'endless setup --install-git-hooks' writes a one-line wrapper at .git/hooks/pre-commit (and other relevant hooks) that invokes the binary. Wrapper is overwriteable with --force. If user has an existing hook, --install-git-hooks --merge appends to it (keep both behaviors).

The binary:
1. Read git env to find branch, .git location.
2. If branch != main, exit 0.
3. If a merge is in progress (MERGE_MSG present), exit 0.
4. If cwd is in a worktree (per .git path), exit 0.
5. Otherwise print actionable error and exit 1.

Same logic as E-1012's Claude Code hook; different invocation surface.

## When to revisit

When any of:
- A real incident shows main was dirtied by something Claude Code didn't catch.
- Endless has non-Claude users.
- A user requests it.

## From the description

Deferred because none of those are current pain points.

Challenges to design through: distribution, composability with existing hooks, cross-platform Windows hostility, --no-verify bypass, worktree handling.

Likely-approach sketch and revisit triggers in the analysis field.

fields.title: Decide the db-ledger growth lifecycle
fields.description: Decide whether the database is always rebuilt from the full ledger, growing linearly, or from periodic checkpoints with ledger truncation, first confirming it isn't already settled.
fields.notes:
Filed 2026-04-30 during E-987 design, when the ledger was still called the 'event log' and lived at .endless/events; the subject is today's .endless/db-ledger.

E-1935's premise leans (A) — every developer rebuilding the projection from the shared ledger — and E-1671/E-1674's upcasting work presumes the full history is kept and replayable, so this may already be answered by the epic it now sits under.
fields.analysis:
Surfaced during E-987 design discussion (2026-04-30). Tomorrow's problem; not blocking E-987 or E-971.

## The question

Two patterns for the projection engine (E-807) when the events log grows:

**Pattern A: Always rebuild from full event log.**
- '.endless/data.sql' is unnecessary; events log is sole source of truth.
- 'endless rebuild-db' replays every event from the beginning.
- Performance scales linearly with event count.
- For solo dev with manageable event-log size, fine for years.
- Simpler architecture: one source of truth, no checkpoint logic.

**Pattern B: Periodic data.sql checkpoint with event-log truncation.**
- 'endless dump' (or similar) creates a checkpoint at .endless/data.sql, then truncates the events log (or starts a new segment, leaving older ones removable).
- Rebuild = checkpoint + remaining events.
- Performance bounded by checkpoint frequency.
- More complex: checkpoint creation, segment retention rules, rebuild-with-checkpoint logic.

## Current state

data.sql exists in the repo (~114KB on 2026-04-30, last updated 2026-04-21 — 9 days stale). It's a periodic dump created by an explicit command, not auto-updated. So we're loosely in Pattern B without the truncation half being implemented.

## What to decide later

1. Is data.sql actually load-bearing (anyone depends on it being a checkpoint) or vestigial (could be deleted today)?
2. What's the events-log growth rate in practice? Measure across a few months to know if Pattern A scales.
3. If Pattern B: how often to checkpoint? What's the segment retention policy? Who triggers it (manual command, hook, daemon)?

## When to revisit

- If 'rebuild-db' becomes painfully slow.
- If events log grows past some threshold (e.g., 100MB, or rebuild > 30s).
- If a fresh-clone workflow needs faster bootstrap than full replay.

## From the description

Confirm that before planning it; if (A) is settled, what remains is only the growth bound, which is a smaller question than the one filed.

fields.title: Add recovery help for rebase conflicts during land
fields.description: Add recovery help for worktree land rebase conflicts on Endless-managed files: document the steps and show a hint in land's rebase-failure error.
fields.notes: Companion to E-987 (auto-commit endless-managed files during land).
fields.context: E-987's land flow rebases the worktree onto main after auto-committing endless-managed files; in normal operation rebase is conflict-free, but corner cases (pre-E-972 worktrees with stale auto-file commits, hand-edits, future code paths writing auto-files from a worktree) will hit eventually.
fields.analysis:
Companion to E-987 (auto-commit endless-managed files during land).

## The case

E-987's land flow rebases the worktree onto main after auto-committing endless-managed files. In normal operation, the rebase has nothing to conflict on — per E-972, all auto-managed files (events log, snapshots) are written to main's location, never the worktree's. Worktree branches don't modify these files, so rebase is conflict-free.

But corner cases will hit eventually:
1. A worktree predates E-972 and has stale auto-file writes baked into commits.
2. Someone hand-edited an auto-file in a worktree (prohibited by E-1017 but enforcement isn't perfect).
3. A future endless feature accidentally writes one of these files from a worktree without going through main's location.

When any of these happen, 'endless worktree land' will fail mid-rebase with a git conflict message. The user needs a recovery path that doesn't require deep git knowledge.

## v1 (this task)

Document the recovery procedure. Probably:

  git rebase --abort
  git checkout main -- <auto-files-with-conflicts>
  endless worktree land <task-id>  # retry

Surface this as part of the rebase-failure error message from 'endless worktree land' (a hint, not just a raw git error).

## v2 (later if needed)

Build an 'endless worktree land --resolve-auto' flag that automates the v1 procedure: detects the conflict is on auto-managed files, takes main's version, retries the rebase. Only safe when the conflict IS on auto files (don't auto-resolve user-work conflicts).

## When to escalate to v2

- If we hit this conflict more than 2-3 times in real use.
- If the documented recovery feels unsafe to type from a hot-key state.

## From the description

v2: 'land --resolve-auto' flag, gated on real recurrence.

fields.title: Populate the companion file's worktree path
fields.description: Populate the session companion file's worktree path from the session's active task when a task starts, so readers stop falling back to the current directory.
fields.context:
The companion file (E-989) has a worktree_path field that is currently never set — writeClaudeCompanion always leaves it empty.

This makes session use (E-1014) and session cd (E-990) fall back to cwd, which for sessions started outside a worktree (like the bootstrap session running in main) does not point at the worktree the user actually wants to test.
fields.analysis:
The companion file (E-989) has a worktree_path field that is currently never set — writeClaudeCompanion always leaves it empty. This makes session use (E-1014) and session cd (E-990) fall back to cwd, which for sessions started outside a worktree (like the bootstrap session running in main) does not point at the worktree the user actually wants to test.

Goal: when a Claude session has an active task with an associated worktree, the companion file's worktree_path reflects that worktree. Readers (session use, session cd, session show) then resolve to the right place automatically, no extra logic in each command.

Where to write it:

Option A — writer side, hook-driven. In cmd/endless-hook/claude.go, on PostToolUse (or UserPromptSubmit) after the session's active_task_id changes (e.g. via 'endless task start'), look up whether .endless/worktrees/e-<task_id>*/ exists; if yes, update the companion file's worktree_path. Single source of truth, all readers benefit.

Option B — reader side, on demand. In session_use_resolve / session_cd_resolve / session_show_resolve, after fetching the companion record, query DB for active_task_id and check filesystem for the worktree. Skip the companion field entirely.

Trade-offs:
- A keeps readers simple, costs a hook change and a small write per task switch.
- B avoids hook churn but duplicates the lookup in every reader.

Recommend A: cleaner long-term, fewer places to keep in sync. The hook-side change is small (a few lines after handlePostToolUseSession's task-start branch).

Worktree naming convention is the filesystem glob '.endless/worktrees/e-<task_id>*' — agreed convention from E-989/E-990 work, formalized in E-971 (which is still blocked but the convention is in active use).

Verification:
- Start a Claude session, run 'endless task start <id>' on a task with a worktree at .endless/worktrees/e-<id>-<slug>/. The companion file's worktree_path updates to that path within the same UserPromptSubmit cycle.
- Switch active task via another 'endless task start <other-id>'. worktree_path updates to the new worktree (or clears if the new task has none).
- 'endless session use' on that session emits cd to the worktree, not the cwd.

Out of scope:
- Formalizing the worktree-naming convention beyond filesystem glob (E-971's domain).
- Cleaning up worktree_path when a task ends (covered by SessionEnd removing the whole companion file).

Origin: E-1014 landing surfaced that worktree_path is dead today. Without this, session use's activation lands at cwd, which for sessions started outside a worktree is the wrong place.

## From the description

Recommendation: writer-side hook update on task-start (option A) — single source of truth, all readers benefit, small hook change. Worktree naming convention: '.endless/worktrees/e-<task_id>*'.

Verification matrix in the analysis field.

fields.title: Fix hook task matchers to accept prefixed task IDs
fields.description: Fix the hook's task start and complete matchers to accept task IDs with their letter prefix as the CLI does, so starting a task that way marks it active.
fields.context: So 'endless task start E-1027' typed in a Bash tool is silently a no-op for the session-state side effect: StartWorkSession never fires, sessions.active_task_id stays NULL.
fields.analysis:
The CLI's TaskIDType (src/endless/cli.py) accepts both 'E-1027' and '1027'. The hook's regex matchers in DEFAULT_MATCHERS (src/endless/matchers.py:75,79) only match bare digits — 'endless\\s+task\\s+start\\s+(\\d+)'. So 'endless task start E-1027' typed in a Bash tool is silently a no-op for the session-state side effect: StartWorkSession never fires, sessions.active_task_id stays NULL.

Discovered while verifying E-1027 (companion worktree_path population): my own session showed active_task_id=NULL despite running 'endless task start E-1027' earlier. Root cause traced to the regex.

Fix: relax both regexes to accept an optional E- (or e-) prefix. Capture group still extracts only digits so claude.go's strconv.ParseInt is unaffected:

  start:    endless\\s+task\\s+start\\s+(?:[Ee]-)?(\\d+)
  complete: endless\\s+task\\s+complete\\s+(?:[Ee]-)?(\\d+)

Two places need updating:
1. src/endless/matchers.py DEFAULT_MATCHERS — fixes future seeds.
2. Existing machine configs (~/.config/endless/config.json) — needs a one-shot migration or manual edit. The seed function only writes DEFAULT_MATCHERS when 'matchers' key is missing; it never updates. Decide: ship a tiny migration in the seed function, or document a one-time manual edit.

Verification:
- Run 'endless task start E-1027' in a Bash tool. sessions.active_task_id is set in DB (was NULL before). Companion file's worktree_path populates if a worktree exists.
- 'endless task start 1027' (bare integer) still works (backward compat).
- 'endless task complete E-1027' likewise.

Out of scope: any other CLI/hook gap where E- prefix is silently dropped. File separately if found.

Origin: E-1027 verification revealed the gap.

## From the description

Fix: relax both regexes to accept an optional [Ee]- prefix; capture group still extracts only digits. Two places: DEFAULT_MATCHERS and existing machine configs (decide migration vs manual edit).

fields.description: Refresh the session companion file on every user prompt, not only when missing, so it is never more than one prompt behind the database.
fields.context:
Today the UserPromptSubmit handler in cmd/endless-hook/claude.go calls writeClaudeCompanion only when CompanionExists returns false (the E-1011 backfill semantic).

That leaves the companion file vulnerable to drift any time active_task_id changes through a path that doesn't trigger writeClaudeCompanion.
fields.analysis:
Today the UserPromptSubmit handler in cmd/endless-hook/claude.go calls writeClaudeCompanion only when CompanionExists returns false (the E-1011 backfill semantic). That leaves the companion file vulnerable to drift any time the active_task_id changes through a path that doesn't trigger writeClaudeCompanion — for example when:

- A multi-command bash invocation contains 'endless task start E-NNN' but the hook's tool_input.command doesn't include the relevant fragment (observed during E-1027/E-1028 verification: the synthetic stdin test fired StartWorkSession correctly while the same command in a multi-command Bash tool invocation did not).
- A user edits sessions.active_task_id directly via sqlite3.
- Any future code path that mutates session state without going through claude.go's PostToolUse handlers.

Symptom: 'endless session use' cd's to a stale worktree path; 'session show' reports stale active task. Easy for a human to misattribute or shrug off.

Fix: change the UserPromptSubmit handler to always call writeClaudeCompanion (drop the CompanionExists guard). Cost: one atomic JSON write per prompt — sub-millisecond. Benefit: the companion file is at most one prompt out of date with the DB regardless of which intermediate hook events fire or miss.

Implementation:
- Replace the 'if !exists { write }' block with an unconditional write.
- writeClaudeCompanion already overwrites atomically (tempfile + rename) — no concurrency concern.
- Delete CompanionExists if no other caller remains; otherwise keep it.

Verification:
- Manually mutate sessions.active_task_id in DB. Submit any prompt. Companion file's worktree_path updates within that turn.
- Run 'endless task start E-NNN' through whatever bash form previously failed to fire the hook. Within one prompt, companion catches up.
- Existing companion-file tests still pass; the backfill behavior subsumes the new always-write behavior.

Origin: E-1027/E-1028 verification surfaced that the hook can miss task-state events depending on Bash tool_input format. Rather than chase that intermittent miss, kill the entire drift class. Mike's question after I 'flagged' it: 'how will we know when it recurs?' — we won't; better to make recurrence harmless.

## From the description

Cost: one atomic JSON write per prompt, sub-millisecond. Benefit: companion at most one prompt out of date with the DB.

Drift scenarios and verification matrix are in the analysis field.

fields.analysis:
Today 'endless session use' emits 5 env vars (ENDLESS_SESSION_ID, ENDLESS_HARNESS_SESSION_ID, ENDLESS_HARNESS, ENDLESS_PROJECT_ROOT, ENDLESS_WORKTREE_PATH) plus a cd. Only the integer id is canonical; the rest are derivable from it via DB. Snapshotting them into env saves an 'endless' lookup per consumer, but at the cost of staleness — exactly the class of bug E-1015 verification surfaced when the worktree was removed mid-turn.

Mike's call: minimal is right. A static value can never be stale if it's never written.

Activation block becomes:

  cd <target>
  export ENDLESS_SESSION_ID=<id>

Where <target> is the worktree path if its directory exists at lookup time, else cwd. Validation is at the point the cd line is emitted — narrow window, no value persisted.

Consumers that need other fields call 'endless session show <id> --json' (already exists, returns the full picture). One process spawn per lookup; trade for guaranteed freshness.

Extension contract changes:
- .endless/extensions/use.sh now receives only ENDLESS_SESSION_ID in its env.
- Extensions that need worktree path / project root / etc. call 'endless session show \$ENDLESS_SESSION_ID --json' and parse with jq.
- Documented as the contract; existing extensions need updating (none in the wild today).

Verification:
- 'endless session use 247' emits exactly two lines: cd and ENDLESS_SESSION_ID export.
- worktree_path at lookup time exists -> cd to it. Doesn't exist -> cd to cwd. Same logic E-1037 wanted.

- 'endless session show \$ENDLESS_SESSION_ID --json' returns same fields as before.

Supersedes E-1037 (worktree_path validation alone is too narrow; the larger fix is the env minimization).

Origin: E-1015 verification + Mike's design call: 'It will never fail for a stale value.'

fields.context:
/usr/local/bin/endless-go is a single global symlink into the MAIN checkout's bin/.

Two neighbours already solved adjacent halves: E-998 points a worktree Claude session's hooks at the worktree's own bin/endless-go hook claude via its .claude/settings.json, and E-1368 made the binary self-detect the sandbox DB from cwd -- but that routes the DATABASE, not which binary runs.
fields.analysis:
REVISED 2026-08-21 (E-1944). The original text was written against endless-event, a binary that no longer exists: E-1367 consolidated the endless-* binaries into a single endless-go with subcommands, so the surface is now 'endless-go event ...' and the only installed symlink is endless-go, pointing into the MAIN checkout's bin/. The original premise -- 'just install from worktree A makes every command hit A's binary' -- is also no longer the live failure: CLAUDE.md now requires just install to run from the main checkout only, so the symlink deliberately points at main.

SCOPE OF THE REMAINING GAP. The worktree binary is already preferred where it has been wired explicitly: E-998 writes an absolute path to <worktree>/bin/endless-go into the worktree's .claude/settings.json, so hooks run candidate code, and invoking ./bin/endless-go directly obviously does too. The gap is NAME-RESOLVED invocation -- the Python CLI dispatching to the Go binary, and anything found via PATH -- which still reaches main's binary from inside a worktree.

RAISED IMPORTANCE. Under ED-1567 and ED-1570 the binary that runs determines which schema version is expected, and a mismatch now HALTS rather than merely behaving stalely. Picking the wrong binary stops being a staleness annoyance and becomes a hard stop.

## From the description

Approaches: (a) prepend ./bin to PATH in shell-init when in a worktree, (b) have the Python CLI auto-detect a worktree-local bin/ and prefer it, mirroring E-1368's cwd self-detection, (c) install per-worktree to alternative paths.

fields.context: The hot path is already Go behind a single consolidated binary (E-1367 superseded the multi-binary layout; the web surface was excised by E-1939).
fields.analysis:
## The port must embed the files Python reads from the source tree (E-2155, 2026-09-17)

Three Python modules resolve data files by walking up from their own file to the
repository root: the guide directory (read by `endless guide` and by the
agent-help map), the lifecycle map, and `schema.sql`. The wheel ships only
`src/endless`, so none of those files exist in a non-editable install: a wheel
built from this tree contains no `docs/`, and `endless guide` — the first command
CLAUDE.md tells an agent to run — fails with "Guide directory not found" under a
plain `pip`, `pipx`, or `uv tool install` without `-e`.

It has not bitten anyone because the only documented install is editable.

Recorded here rather than fixed in Python, because the port is where it goes
away: Go already embeds `schema.sql`, the migrations and the templates with
`go:embed`, and the ported `guide` should embed the guide the same way. Worth an
explicit check when `guide` and the status vocabulary move, plus a test that the
built artifact — not the source tree — can render the guide.

## From the description

Settled: the end state is ONE binary named endless, and no transitional second command set is needed — every name the two surfaces share today is a Python shim in front of the Go implementation, so merging deletes the shim rather than reconciling a conflict.

Settled: once the port starts, no new Python work lands in the files being ported (task_cmd, cli, worktree_cmd, session_cmd); anything still open at that point is re-filed against the Go implementation rather than carrying a patch with nowhere to land.

Still open: whether internal plumbing (event, hook, sandbox, template, markdown) stays visible in help once the binary is user-facing.

fields.analysis:
# Concrete call site: the post-land reap sweep

Added 2026-08-21 from ES-1127 (E-1696), which hit this live.

`_reap_stale_worktrees` (src/endless/worktree_cmd.py) resolves its binary
with `shutil.which("endless-go")` — one of the "other shutil.which sites" this
task's description names for E-1039's refactor. It is worth calling out
specifically because it is the one where the stale-global choice is GUARANTEED
to be wrong, not merely possibly wrong.

## Why this site is special

The land already pins its DB-touching steps to the worktree binary
(`_resolve_land_endless_go`, E-1664): for a self_dev land, apply-change and
record-landing must use the build whose embedded schema and enums match the
rows they are writing. The reap sweep runs from inside `endless worktree land`
AFTER apply-change, against the same real DB — and was never pinned.

So on any land carrying an enum-seeding migration, the sequence is:

    endless worktree land  → apply migration      (real DB now ahead)
                           → reap sweep           ✗ integrity check fails
    just land wrapper      → main moved → just build
                                                  (window closes)

Observed on the E-1696 land:

    endless-go event: reap-worktrees: db: session_task_relations integrity
    check on ~/.config/endless/endless.db: sessiontaskrelation:
    session_task_relations row id=4 slug="referenced" has no matching enum
    constant

Non-fatal (the call site catches and prints), self-healing (the wrapper's
`just build` closes the window seconds later), and harmless (the sweep is
TTL-based garbage collection with four triggers, so a missed sweep only defers
reaping). But it prints an alarming failure on exactly the lands where a user is
least equipped to dismiss it.

## Why it must not be fixed locally

Bolting an `endless_go_bin` parameter onto `_reap_stale_worktrees` would work —
`endless_go_bin` is already in scope at the call site (computed at
worktree_cmd.py, reap at :2461) and the other three callers
(two post-claim paths in task_cmd.py, plus `endless worktree reap`) legitimately
want the global. But that is a hand-rolled exception at precisely one of the
sites this helper exists to make uniform, and E-1039 would then have to unpick
it rather than replace a plain `shutil.which` call.

## What this implies for the helper's shape

`resolve_endless_bin_dir()` as described detects worktree-local `bin/` and falls
back to the PATH first match. This site needs slightly more than a cwd-derived
answer: during a land the correct binary belongs to the worktree being landed,
which is not necessarily the caller's cwd, and for a NON-self_dev project the
global is correct and no worktree binary exists at all
(`_resolve_land_endless_go` returns None for that case). Either the helper takes
an explicit worktree hint, or the land keeps its own resolver and the helper
covers the cwd-derived majority — worth deciding before E-1039 sweeps the call
sites, since this one cannot be answered from cwd alone.

## Sequencing note

Under E-2020 (E-1944 decision 3) a binary opening a DB ahead of it HALTS, for
any binary, permanently. So this failure is not something to suppress — it is
the designed guard working. The only real fix is never invoking a stale binary
in that window, which is binary selection, which is this task.

## From the description

Detects worktree-local bin/, falls back to PATH first match.

fields.title: Design a strategy to store session-learned rules in the repo
fields.description: Design a strategy for writing project-level rules learned in sessions into the repo, alongside personal memory, so they reach other machines, other AI harnesses, human users and fresh sessions.
fields.context:
Per-session AI memory (~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/MEMORY.md and friends) only helps the same Claude instance with that memory directory. It does not reach: other Claude sessions on other machines, other AI harnesses (Codex, etc.), human users of endless-the-product, or future fresh sessions that haven't accumulated those rules.

Yet many learned rules are project-level — they describe how endless's workflow is meant to work, not personal user preferences.

Examples surfaced in 2026-05-01 conversation:
- 'Long-form task content goes in .endless/plans/E-NNN.md attached via --text; description stays a 2-3 sentence pitch.'
- 'The session that creates a plan file owns committing it.'

Both are about endless's plan workflow.

(User's global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md already has a pattern: 'After ANY correction from the user: update ~/.claude/LESSONS.md with the pattern.' That's user-scoped. Project-scoped equivalent would be e.g. .endless/lessons/ or project-LESSONS.md.)

Origin: 2026-05-01 conversation. Mike: 'create a task for another session to work on that come up with a strategy to write learnings to the endless repo in parallel with memory. This may be unique to the endless project itself, or maybe it is a general lessons feature that all projects could use.'
fields.analysis:
Open question: project-specific feature, or general 'lessons' infrastructure all endless-managed projects could use?

Considerations / things to weigh:
- Where do learnings live? .endless/learnings/<topic>.md? .endless/conventions.md? Inline in quick-start guide? Repo-level CLAUDE.md? Multiple?
- Mike's pushback (2026-05-01): 'CLAUDE.md does not work because everyone's CLAUDE.md may be different.' Repo-rooted CLAUDE.md is shared, but users may override or omit it; can't rely on it as authoritative.
- Auto-propagation vs. manual: should there be tooling (e.g. 'endless lesson add') that captures a rule and writes it to the repo? Or just a convention agents follow?
- How does an agent/user discover existing lessons? Surface in 'endless quick-start'? A new 'endless lessons' command?
- Distinguish project-level rules (apply to all who work on this project) from personal rules (apply to this user's preferences). The latter still belongs in personal memory only.
- Migration path: rules already in personal memory that should also be in the repo — how do they get there?

Out of scope for this design task:
- Implementing the chosen strategy (file follow-up once design lands).
- Migrating existing personal-memory rules into the repo (separate task).

fields.analysis: Fix: setpgid the subshell, signal the whole group on enter exit and on signal handler. Also consider blocking destroy when the sandbox has live writers, with a clear error pointing at the offender.

fields.title: Fix session use sibling-pane lookup in same tmux window
fields.description: Fix endless session use so, run from a tmux pane, it finds the running Claude pane in the same window instead of reporting that no sibling exists.
fields.context: On 2026-05-02, 'eval "$(endless session use)"' from a tmux pane in the same window as the Claude Code pane reported 'No sibling Claude pane in this tmux window. Run `endless session list` to see all candidates project-wide.' The sibling Claude pane was demonstrably running in the same window.
fields.analysis:
Investigate the pane-discovery logic: tmux query, env-var matching (TMUX_PANE), or the heuristic for what counts as a 'Claude pane'.

Likely related to how Claude's process tree or env is identified across sessions.

fields.title: Fix Python db._migrate to tolerate empty DB
fields.description: Fix the Python schema migration so it tolerates an empty database instead of failing with 'no such table: tasks' on fresh installs and in sandboxes.
fields.context: Surfaces inside E-1074 sandbox shells (and on fresh installs) when a Go binary creates the DB file before Python's is_new check. Will block E-1078 pytest fixture on every fresh sandbox.

fields.title: Move verbs out of the generic matchers in config
fields.description: Move verbs out of the generic matcher list into a top-level verbs array of value and definition, with its own endless verb command group; other matcher types stay generic.
fields.analysis:
Verbs are domain-special: they carry definitions (and potentially aliases, examples) that other matcher types do not. Stuffing 'definitions' as a sibling field on the generic matcher object coupled type-specific content into the schema.

Shared matching engine stays shared.

fields.title: Fix a migration flipping relation directions on every run
fields.description: Fix the schema migration that swaps source and target on blocks and replaces relations so it runs once, instead of flipping their direction on every endless command.
fields.notes:
Pre-existing data corruption from past flips was repaired manually post-patch.

E-863 (proper schema version migration system) is the structural fix that would have prevented this.
fields.context:
src/endless/db.py:_migrate_v5 contains two UPDATE statements that swap source/target on rows where dep_type IN ('needs','blocks') and where dep_type='replaces'.

Result: data corruption — at any moment, ~half of rows are in their intended direction and ~half are inverted, depending on parity of past invocations.

Symptoms originally observed as inconsistent labels in 'task show' / 'task relations' / 'task detail' for the same task; the labels were correct, the underlying data was flapping.
fields.analysis: Fix: gate the swap UPDATEs on PRAGMA user_version; set user_version=5 once V5 has run. Audit existing data afterwards (5 replaces rows + 60 blocks rows).

fields.title: Consider a not-applicable phase for terminal statuses
fields.description: Consider adding a phase value such as not-applicable or none for tasks in a terminal status like obsolete or confirmed.

fields.title: Show old -> new values on state-mutating task commands
fields.description: Show changed fields as '<label>: <old> -> <new>' on every task command that changes state, such as confirm, update and start, so users see what changed and how to revert.
fields.notes: Replaces E-973.

fields.title: Validate task add --phase at parse time
fields.description: Validate task add --phase at parse time against the allowed phases, like the other --phase options, so bad values never reach the event layer.
fields.context: The asymmetry means bad values reach the events layer before being rejected (E-1101 catches them, but with a worse error).
fields.analysis: One-line fix: add the type to task add's --phase decorator.

fields.title: Migrate machine-layer verbs into the project config
fields.description: Migrate all verb entries from the machine-layer config into the project's config, deduplicated by value, leaving the machine layer intact for other projects.
fields.analysis:
Verbs accumulated in the machine layer during endless work were derived from this project and should travel with the repo.

Machine layer left intact so other projects on this machine still have access via the merge.

fields.title: Define collision strategy for short-id session worktrees
fields.description: Define how to avoid branch-name collisions when session worktrees are named with a short prefix of the session ID: a longer prefix, the full ID, or a random suffix.
fields.context: If Layer F creates session-flavor worktrees using a short-id prefix of the session UUID (e.g. first 8 chars), branch name collisions are theoretically possible across sessions sharing that prefix.
fields.analysis:
Decide: retry with longer prefix? Use full UUID? Random suffix?

Layer D itself doesn't create worktrees so this is purely a Layer F concern; recording it as a maybe so it isn't forgotten.

fields.title: Extract verbs from config.json into verbs.json
fields.description: Extract verbs from config.json into their own verbs.json files at project and machine level, migrating existing entries on first load.
fields.context: After E-1117 + E-1122, verbs dominate the config file (80+ entries) and obscure the config-oriented fields (roots, ignore, ownership, etc.).
fields.analysis: Top-level JSON array of {value, definition} objects. Migration extracts existing 'verbs' key from config.json on first load. Verb-gate validation reads from new path.

fields.title: Add commands that show tmux window and task lineage
fields.description: Add CLI commands that show which tmux window spawned the current one, the tasks the current window worked on, and how they relate to tasks in sibling windows.
fields.analysis:
The tmux integration itself is separate; this task is just the data-side CLI surface so the status-line script has something to call.

Likely shape: 'endless session lineage', 'endless session tasks', 'endless session siblings' — names TBD.

fields.title: Add a per-prompt active-task reminder and topic-change gate
fields.description: Add a hook that reminds the agent of its active task on every prompt and, when a prompt signals a topic change, blocks file edits until a task is claimed, confirmed or added.
fields.notes:
Layer E of E-971: behavioral gate.

See attached prompt for full scope and acceptance criteria; design in .endless/plans/E-971.md (Behavioral gate section).
fields.analysis: PreToolUse extended to also block Write/Edit when gate is pending. Gate cleared by 'endless task start/confirm/add' verbs.

fields.title: Add 'endless task assume' command
fields.description: Add an endless task assume command that, like task confirm, closes a task, marking its behavior as believed correct rather than verified.

fields.title: Record spawn lineage on endless task spawn
fields.description: Record which tmux window spawned a new one on endless task spawn, both as a tmux option on the new window and in the database linking the spawned task to the spawning session.
fields.notes: Pairs with E-1125 (read-side CLI).
fields.context:
endless task spawn currently sets @endless_task_id and @endless_project_id on the new tmux window but does not capture the spawning window.

Surfaced 2026-05-02 when Mike got lost finding his way back from spawned sessions.

fields.title: Verify Claude Code hook merge-vs-replace semantics
fields.description: Verify whether Claude Code merges or replaces hook config across user, project and local settings, since worktree hook routing assumed it replaces.
fields.context: E-998 was built on the assumption of replace; if it's merge, a session inside a worktree fires both the worktree binary and the global, doubling state-mutating hook work.

fields.title: Stop the global hook duplicating work in worktree sessions
fields.description: Stop the global endless-hook from doing work in a worktree session when the worktree has its own hook binary, so each event is handled once instead of twice.
fields.context: E-998 created per-worktree .claude/settings.json so worktree-cwd Claude sessions fire bin/endless-hook.
fields.analysis: Fix: at endless-hook startup, walk up cwd for .endless/worktree.json; if found and the worktree's bin/endless-hook exists and is a different inode than os.Args[0], log+exit 0 without doing work. Worktree binary handles the event alone.

fields.title: Add new --as value to 'endless task link'
fields.description: Add a new relation-type value for endless task link --as.
Add an --analysis flag to the task update command.
Add a --notes flag to the task update command.
Add a --worktree <path> option to endless task spawn so the new tmux window starts in that worktree and the spawned Claude session uses its settings and hooks.
fields.notes: Required for the worktree-spawn coordinator pattern (sibling task on routing/dispatch).
fields.context: Currently spawn cd's the new tmux window to the project's main checkout path before launching claude, so the spawned session reads main's .claude/settings.json at startup — defeating the worktree-aware hook override produced by 'just claude-settings-init'.

fields.title: Add coordinator that spawns per-task worktree sessions
fields.description: Add a long-running coordinator that watches a task filter and, for each task, creates a worktree, spawns a Claude session, waits for completion, lands on approval and moves to the next.
fields.context: Replaces dedicating a human-spawned orchestrator session to this role.
fields.analysis:
Intent clarified 2026-06-10 by Mike: the long-running command is a Go/Python loop (daemon), NOT a Claude session orchestrator. It dispatches Claude sessions deterministically with no Claude tokens consumed on the deterministic management aspects (claim/wait/land cadence). Relates_to E-1552, which is the alternative interactive Claude-session-based orchestrator pattern using Agent View (dispatches Claude background sessions, monitored from one screen, human in the loop). The two may co-exist (E-1136 is 'walk away,' E-1552 is 'stay at one screen'), OR Agent View may obsolete E-1136, OR E-1136 may turn out to be the more robust longer-term path because deterministic management belongs in code, not in a Claude conversation. The relationship/sequencing decision is part of E-1552's scope.

## From the description

Naming and design (route/dispatch/orchestrate/spawn-extension, completion detection, approval gating, concurrency) to be decided in the plan, informed by operational experience running this manually first.

fields.title: Restore cwd-walk resolution for project config paths
fields.description: Restore walking up from the current directory to find project config.json and verbs.json, so writes from a worktree go to its own files and writes from main go to main's.
fields.notes: Per the new decision reversing E-1112:
fields.analysis:
writes from a worktree go to the worktree's project files; writes from main go to main's. Affects project_config_path() and project_verbs_path() in src/endless/matchers.py and any callers that assumed E-1111's anchor-to-main semantics.

Verification: from a worktree, run 'endless verb add foo'; only the worktree's .endless/verbs.json is modified, not main's; the new verb still surfaces in subsequent reads via project + machine layer merge.

fields.title: Update land auto-commit list and dedup verbs.json
fields.description: Update worktree land to auto-commit .endless/verbs.json instead of config.json, merging the worktree's verbs with main's by set union and skipping the commit when nothing changes.
fields.notes: Per the auto-commit-inversion decision (modifies E-1056):
fields.analysis:
The auto-commit step for verbs.json reads main's verbs.json, performs additive set-union on the value key against the worktree's verbs.json, writes the deduped result, and commits to the worktree's branch. If the post-dedup result equals main's content, skip the commit (no-op). All in Go code (cmd/endless-event or wherever the land flow lives); no .gitattributes merge driver.

Verification: two worktrees independently add the same verb; first lands cleanly; second lands with auto-commit producing a no-op for verbs.json.

fields.title: Add 'endless decision link' for typed decision relations
fields.description: Add endless decision link and unlink commands with reverses/reversed_by and modifies/modified_by relation types for typed decision-to-decision relationships.
fields.notes: Implement the vocabulary locked in E-1156:
fields.analysis:
Schema reuses task_deps; column is permissive per E-958, no migration.

'clarifies' and 'reaffirms' deferred to maybe-phase E-1157 per YAGNI.

Acceptance also includes retyping the existing prose-typed links from the E-1134 verb-storage thread: E-1140 → E-1112 ('documents' → 'reverses') and E-1141 → E-1056 ('documents' → 'modifies') using the new CLI.

fields.title: Clear the session's active task when confirming from a shell
fields.description: Clear the session's active task whenever a task is confirmed, including when endless task confirm runs directly in a terminal rather than through Claude's hook.
fields.context:
After E-1126's complete→confirm rename, the hook's PostToolUse handler clears sessions.active_task_id when Claude runs 'endless task confirm <id>' as a Bash tool call. But Python's complete_item (src/endless/task_cmd.py) does the underlying DB writes and never touches the session row.

Surfaced during E-1126 verification.
fields.analysis: Fix: have complete_item null active_task_id for any session whose active_task_id matches the just-confirmed task.

fields.title: Add tier column and --tier flag to 'task search'
fields.description: Add a tier column and a --tier filter to the task search command.

fields.title: Rename spawned tmux windows to project, slug and task ID
fields.description: Rename the tmux window task spawn creates from a 30-character title slug to project, slug and task ID, so parallel spawned sessions are easy to tell apart.

fields.title: Add 'cleans_up'/'cleaned_up_by' task relation type
fields.description: Add a cleans_up/cleaned_up_by task relation type for cleanup work that becomes possible or necessary after a parent task ships, distinct from blocks.
fields.context: Origin: 2026-05-03 discussion under E-1134's verb-storage thread; concrete example is the post-ship cleanup pattern (e.g. retyping E-1140/E-1141 prose-typed links) that currently has nowhere clean to live.
fields.analysis:
Motivation: cleanup folded into a parent task gets 'test passes, ship it' treatment from agents and quietly dies; making it its own task with an explicit relation gives it independent visibility (task active, task complete validation, etc.).

Implementation: add the relation type to canonical dep_types (column is permissive per E-958, no migration), wire into 'endless task link' / 'task add --cleans-up' / 'task show' display. Schema reuses task_deps.

fields.title: Allow comma-separated IDs in 'task add --relates-to'
fields.description: Allow the --relates-to flag of task add to take multiple comma-separated task IDs.
Allow the --relates-to flag on the task link command.

fields.description: Rename the relation-type flag from --as to --type on endless task link and task unlink, with no --as alias.
fields.notes: Per E-1148:
fields.analysis:
Affects only src/endless/cli.py (link) and cli.py (unlink) — confirmed via grep that no other --as references exist in src/ or tests/. Update help text.

Verification: 'endless task link E-A --to E-B --type blocks' creates the relation; 'endless task unlink E-A --to E-B --type blocks' removes it; --as raises a click 'No such option' error (no alias).

Out of scope: E-1139's 'endless decision link' will adopt --type natively without going through --as first.

fields.title: Add worktree auto-creation to 'task start'

fields.title: Detect worktree context in endless cwd-walk
fields.description: Detect when endless runs inside a git worktree and use the main checkout's database or refuse with a clear error, instead of connecting to an empty database in the worktree.
fields.context: Discovered 2026-05-03 verifying E-1114 from its own worktree.
fields.analysis: Detect the worktree case (git rev-parse --git-common-dir or presence of .endless/worktrees/<name>/ ancestry) and either anchor to the main checkout's .endless/ or refuse with a clear error pointing at the fix.

fields.description: Add an endless session forget command that unsets the variables session use exported, plus an esf shell helper, so a shell can leave an activated session.
fields.context:
esu (eval $(endless session use)) exports ENDLESS_PROJECT_ROOT, ENDLESS_WORKTREE_PATH, ENDLESS_SESSION_ID, ENDLESS_HARNESS_SESSION_ID, ENDLESS_HARNESS into the current shell. There is no inverse — esp only cd's to the project root, it does not unset the vars.

Result: every subsequent endless command in that shell points at the activated session's worktree DB until the user opens a new shell or manually unsets all five vars.

Discovered 2026-05-03 verifying E-1114.

fields.title: Replace missing/empty DB traceback with actionable error
fields.description: Replace the raw traceback shown when the database is missing or has no tables with a message naming the database path and how to fix it.
fields.context:
Common triggers: (a) ENDLESS_PROJECT_ROOT/ENDLESS_WORKTREE_PATH env vars from a stale esu activation pointing at a worktree's empty .endless/, (b) cwd-walk landing in a worktree whose .endless/ has no DB (see E-1158).

esp itself crashes on this path too — fixing the diagnostic auto-fixes esp's UX. Discovered 2026-05-03 verifying E-1114.
fields.analysis: Catch sqlite3.OperationalError at the db.query boundary and re-raise as a friendly message naming the resolved DB path, the resolution mechanism (env var vs cwd-walk), and the recovery (cd elsewhere, unset ENDLESS_*, or run init).

fields.title: Update 'session use' docs to match single-var activation
fields.description: Update the session use command's help and its design plan to say activation only changes directory and exports the session ID, not five variables.
fields.context:
E-1038 (commit 9ea22b3, 2026-05-01) reduced 'endless session use' activation from five ENDLESS_* exports to one (ENDLESS_SESSION_ID + cd). Quote from that commit: 'It will never fail for a stale value. Minimal wins.'

The CODE (src/endless/session_cmd.py, session_use_resolve) correctly emits only the two lines.

Discovered 2026-05-03 when Claude (me) read the cli.py docstring and confidently told Mike that esu exports five vars, propagating the lie. Symptom for users: stale docs make it look like a regression has shipped when it hasn't.
fields.analysis: Fix: trim the cli.py docstring to match reality (cd + ENDLESS_SESSION_ID), and add an 'Updated by E-1038' note at the top of E-1014.md plus a callout in the affected section.

fields.title: Refuse endless commands inside an endless-sandbox subshell
fields.description: Refuse endless commands run inside an endless-sandbox subshell with an error naming the sandbox, except an explicit allowlist such as --help and --version.
fields.notes: Sibling of E-1160.
fields.analysis: Allowlist beats deny-list because future subcommands inherit refusal automatically.

fields.title: Document clearing of vars set by use.sh extensions
fields.description: Document the options for clearing environment variables that user-written session extensions export when leaving a session, and pick one if the leakage becomes a real problem.
fields.notes: References: E-1014 (extension hooks), E-1038 (single-var reduction), E-1159 (esf implementation).
fields.context:
esf (E-1159) clears only the env vars that 'endless session use' is documented to export — currently just ENDLESS_SESSION_ID per E-1038. A user-authored .endless/extensions/use.sh (E-1014) can export arbitrary additional vars (e.g., PATH alterations, NVM_DIR, project-specific exports).

esf has no way to know what an extension set, so those leak.
fields.analysis: Possible approaches to investigate: (a) symmetric extensions/forget.sh that authors maintain alongside use.sh; (b) protocol where use.sh emits a sentinel line listing what it set, captured by esu and replayed by esf; (c) snapshot env before/after esu and diff at esf time. Each has trade-offs.

fields.title: Route shell helpers to the session's worktree CLI
fields.description: Route the esu, esp and esf shell helpers to the endless CLI in the active session's worktree instead of the global install, with clearer errors when a helper or session is missing.
fields.context:
esu/esp/esf call bare 'endless' which resolves to the global CLI.

New subcommands added in a worktree (like 'session forget' from E-1159) aren't reachable via helpers until the worktree is merged and globally installed.

Discovered 2026-05-03 verifying E-1159.
fields.analysis: Use.sh can route but shouldn't be a baseline requirement — users in non-endless-source projects shouldn't have to author a shell extension just for esf to work.

fields.title: Rename .endless/events to .endless/db-ledger
fields.description: Rename the .endless/events directory to .endless/db-ledger so its files read as the authoritative database record rather than discardable logs, migrating existing installs.
fields.context: The 'events' directory naming caused near-data-loss during E-1170's land: those JSONL files are the Endless DB write-ahead record (replay-source for DB rebuild), but their name reads as 'logs' so they were treated as discardable.
fields.analysis:
'journal' has the same problem (cf. systemd journalctl).

ledger and entries are canonical accounting terms; losing one is catastrophic in every domain that uses them.

Migration spans Go writer (cmd/endless-event), Python bridge (event_bridge.py), DB replay/rebuild logic, hooks that scan the path, tests, and a one-time directory rename for existing installs with backward-compat read window.

Open at plan time: keep current host-fp+sequence identifier vs. switch to UUIDs.

fields.title: Prevent direct Write/Edit of plan files
fields.description: Prevent agents from writing or editing plan files directly, in main or a worktree's copy, and direct them to update the task's text through the CLI instead.
fields.notes: Broadened from 'main working tree only' to fold in the plan-files-via-task-update lesson (no hand-edit of the mirror in ANY worktree).
fields.context: Converts lessons no-plan-files-in-main + plan-files-via-task-update.
fields.analysis:
tasks.text is authoritative; the mirror rides to main via worktree-land, never a direct write.

The gate blocks only Claude Write/Edit tool calls; the CLI materialization is unaffected, so the land-produces-plan-markdown flow is intact.

On completion: prune feedback_no_plan_files_in_main.md + feedback_plan_files_via_task_update.md + their MEMORY.md index lines.

fields.description: Move plan snapshots from one flat directory into per-task subdirectories, so all snapshots for a task can be found in one place.
fields.context:
Currently .endless/plans/snapshots/ is a flat directory with <timestamp>-<hash>.{json,md} files written by the PostToolUse hook (cmd/endless-hook/claude.go).

To find all captures for a given task, you have to read each .json's metadata to filter by task ID.
fields.analysis:
Snapshots without a task ID go to .endless/plans/snapshots/<session-id>/ (every snapshot is written from a session, so session-id is the always-available fallback).

Migration: one-time move of existing flat-layout snapshots into the new tree based on each .json's metadata.

fields.title: Record each db-ledger write in git immediately
fields.description: Record each database ledger write in a git commit as it happens, instead of letting ledger files pile up uncommitted on main until the next worktree land.
fields.context:
Today .endless/events/*.jsonl (and after E-1197, .endless/db-ledger/db-entries-*.jsonl) only get committed when 'endless worktree land' runs — they accumulate uncommitted on main between landings.

Result: any session that runs endless commands fills the working tree with uncommitted database write-ahead state, which then needs cleanup before any subsequent land.

Sooner-than-later priority because the current friction blocks landing.
fields.analysis:
Optimization to evaluate at plan time: for commits that haven't been pushed to origin yet, amend successive auto-commits into a single rolling commit.

Bounds the commit count without weakening data integrity (each event still becomes part of git history at write time; the amend just rewrites how recent unpushed history is grouped).

fields.title: Validate plan-file path against the task's worktree
fields.description: Validate that a plan-file path given to task update --text is inside the task's active worktree, rejecting others with an error naming the canonical location.
fields.analysis:
Optional partner: 'endless plan new <task-id>' that writes a stub at the canonical path so agents/humans don't have to compute it.

Once shipped, retire the per-Claude memory ~/.claude/projects/-Users-mikeschinkel-Projects-endless/memory/feedback_commit_plan_files_you_create.md — it becomes redundant with the product enforcement.

fields.description: Record verbs.json changes in their own commit as soon as endless verb add runs, instead of leaving the working tree dirty until a manual commit or the next land.
fields.context:
Today 'endless verb add <name>' modifies .endless/verbs.json without committing.

Result: every verb addition leaves the working tree dirty until either (a) someone manually commits, or (b) the next 'endless worktree land' bundles it into the auto-record commit.
fields.analysis:
Both are bad: (a) creates a coordination tax across sessions, (b) couples verbs.json updates to unrelated worktree-land timing.

The verb registry is global config — repo-tracked so all sessions/users on this project benefit from discovered verbs, and machine-stored so verbs are available outside project context.

Both layers required by design.

Direct commit-to-main from verb_add is allowed under E-1199's global-config exception.

fields.title: Fix worktree land failing to remove the worktree dir
fields.description: Fix worktree land so it clears the untracked per-worktree state files and removes the worktree directory cleanly, instead of failing at the final removal step.
fields.notes: Related: E-1009 (gitignore both), E-1195 (review whether the lock-file model itself stays).
fields.context:
because per-worktree state files in `.endless/` are intentionally untracked: `worktree.json` (companion file, never committed because committing it would rotate every worktree's contents whenever another is created/destroyed) and `worktree.lock` (ownership marker per E-971; SessionEnd hook is supposed to delete it but in practice it survives — observed on E-1186 land 2026-05-09).

Land currently surfaces this as a non-fatal error and tells the user to run `git worktree remove` manually.
fields.analysis:
Better: have land explicitly remove both files before `git worktree remove`, or pass `--force` when only those files remain.

Either way the user shouldn't see a spurious error every land.

fields.title: Remove legacy ledger migration code from Go events package
fields.description: Remove the now-dead legacy ledger migration and old-path reader fallback from the Go events package, plus the old auto-commit pattern, since the ledger directory rename is done.
fields.context: After the one-time E-1197 migration script (executed 2026-05-09) renamed .endless/events/ → .endless/db-ledger/ in main and all worktrees and refreshed worktree binaries, the Go-side defensive code becomes dead weight: internal/events/migration.go (MigrateLegacyLedger + helpers), the call from internal/events/writer.go::NewWriter, and the legacy-path scan in internal/events/reader.go::ReadAllEvents.
fields.analysis:
Also remove '.endless/events/*.jsonl' from AUTO_COMMIT_GLOBS in src/endless/worktree_cmd.py — that pattern is dead since no events.jsonl files exist anywhere anymore.

In the wild (fresh clones) no one ever has a .endless/events/ to migrate from, so this code only existed to handle Mike's local environment, which is now settled.

fields.title: Delete merged task branches automatically
fields.description: Delete a task branch's local ref automatically after it lands on main, instead of relying on sessions to remember to do it.
fields.context: Per decision E-1211, after a task/* or e-* branch lands on main, the local ref should be deleted.
fields.analysis:
Likely surface: extend 'endless worktree land' (or whatever lands a task branch) to delete the local branch after a successful merge, AND/OR a post-merge git hook installed by 'endless worktree' setup.

Open question: silent-default-on, or require explicit --delete-branch?

Prefer silent-default since the decision is unambiguous; the action mirrors 'git branch -d' safety (refuses unmerged).

fields.title: Design handling of user-produced dirty state in main
fields.description: Design how Endless handles uncommitted changes and direct commits users make in main so they never block adoption, including a startup tip and a command that moves those changes into a fresh worktree.
fields.context: Endless and Claude have hard rules (E-1199, E-1200, E-1204) against direct commits or dirty session-work state in main.
fields.analysis:
Detect via existing CLAUDECODE / ENDLESS_SESSION_ID env vars (no new vars).

Mechanisms: (1) startup tip when main has any dirty state pointing to 'endless worktree move'; (2) 'endless worktree move' command that lifts uncommitted changes from main into a fresh worktree, leaving main clean; (3) reject pre-commit hooks as a mechanism (not composable, agreed elsewhere).

Goal: zero-friction adoption — users get value without changing behavior, and behavioral shifts happen voluntarily as they see the tooling.

Note: 'move' chosen over 'extract' (read as removing FROM a worktree), aligns with git's vocab via 'git worktree move'.

fields.description: Move plan-file writes from task update --text into the task's active worktree instead of always into main, so plans reach main only when the worktree lands.
fields.notes: Affects E-1169's plan-in-main precondition.
fields.context:
endless task update --text always writes plan files to main's .endless/plans/ via _write_task_plan_file -> _project_root_for_task (task_cmd.py), regardless of cwd or active worktree.

This bit us in 2026-05 when another session created plan files for E-1164/E-1182/E-1186/E-1190 on main while working in worktrees, blocking subsequent landings of E-1170 and E-1197 with stash dances that risked data loss.
fields.analysis: Open at plan time: detection (task-id->worktree map vs. cwd), pre-worktree case (plan mode before task start), read paths (task show / detail --text), existing-file migration.

fields.description: Add a --project flag to endless task update, and any other task subcommand lacking it, so it works when the current directory is not inside a registered project.
fields.context:
Other task subcommands (add, list, detail, link) work from any cwd — they default to a registered project.

`endless task update` is the outlier: when cwd isn't in a registered project directory (e.g., shell cwd dangles after `git worktree remove`), it errors with 'Not in a registered project directory. Specify a name: endless task <command> --project <name>' but does NOT actually accept --project.

Observed during E-1186 wrap-up 2026-05-09 after the worktree dir was removed mid-session.

fields.title: Stop tracking worktree.json and worktree.lock in main
fields.description: Stop tracking the per-worktree worktree.json and worktree.lock files in main by gitignoring them and deleting the stale copies committed there.
fields.notes: Related to E-1195 (lock ownership-model review) but distinct: this is a tracking bug, not a staleness-detection design question.
fields.context: Consequences: (1) every new worktree from main inherits the stale companion; Layer F's create_task_worktree overwrites it locally, which then shows as M in 'git status' and makes 'endless worktree land' fail at the worktree-removal step; (2) the PreToolUse hook's walk-up from cwd finds the companion in main and treats main as a worktree, causing sibling sessions to claim a .endless/worktree.lock there (PID 54419 in the current case); (3) any session in main hits a 'worktree owned by another session' refusal on Edit.
fields.analysis: Fix: add both files to .gitignore, 'git rm --cached .endless/worktree.json' from main, delete the orphan .endless/worktree.lock in main.

fields.title: Rename 'task start' to 'task claim' and add 'task release'
fields.description: Rename task start to task claim to reflect exclusive ownership, and add task release to clear the current session's task binding without ending the session.
fields.notes: Relates to E-1203 (which created the refusal that makes the rename matter).
fields.analysis:
The verb 'start' suggests 'begin work', which is permissive — but the operation actually enforces exclusive ownership (per E-1203's refusal of concurrent live sessions).

'claim' telegraphs that semantic accurately; users hitting the refusal get an outcome consistent with the verb.

Implementation: rename click command and start_item() → claim_item(); add release click command + release_item() that clears sessions.active_task_id for the current session via event emission, leaves tasks.status unchanged, leaves worktree intact.

No 'start' alias (per no-legacy-code rule) unless explicitly requested.

Update verb registry, CLAUDE.md references, and test names.

fields.title: Refuse 'task claim' on a verify-status task without --force
fields.description: Refuse task claim on a task in verify status unless --force is given, instead of silently demoting it back to in progress.

Fix: in claim_item, if target task status is 'verify' (or any of {confirmed, declined, obsolete}), refuse with a message like 'E-NNN is in verify; pass --force to re-claim and demote to in_progress.'

Or for verify specifically, print a notice and proceed (lower friction).

Mike's call which behavior.

fields.description: Add a second tmux status line showing the current Endless task ID, with hotkey and right-click popup menus for common task actions.

Today ships two verbs: `endless tmux apply` (ephemeral apply — configures the running tmux server in one shot; survives until tmux server restart) and `endless tmux status-line` (the runtime printer tmux invokes from `status-format[1]` on each refresh).

Permanent install, color theming, lineage breadcrumbs, and richer menu content land as child tasks.

fields.title: Stop the worktree lookup matching the project root
fields.description: Stop the worktree lookup from treating the project root as a worktree when a stray companion file exists there.
fields.notes: NOTE: the fix was already implemented and tested on the E-1219 branch (task/1219-audit-find-worktree-root) within scope-creep
