fields.title: Create worktree.json on task start in a bare git worktree
fields.description: Create the worktree.json companion file when endless task start runs in a git worktree that lacks one, instead of refusing.
fields.context:
Post-E-1218, .endless/worktree.json is gitignored and not tracked in main.

New worktrees created via 'git worktree add' directly (vs. 'endless task spawn' or 'endless worktree add') do not get a companion file written.

Workaround: write the companion manually before running task start.

Surfaced during E-1209 and E-1219 setup — hit it twice in one session.
fields.analysis: Proposed fix: have endless task start auto-create the companion when (a) the cwd is a registered git worktree under .endless/worktrees/, (b) no companion file exists, (c) the task ID being claimed has no other registered worktree.

fields.description: Add a terminal completed status for tasks whose deliverable is text or findings, such as audits, research and reviews, allowed only for verbs flagged completable and requiring an outcome.
fields.notes: See plan text for design rationale and starter verb list.
fields.analysis: Gate via `completable: true` flag in verbs.json + require `--outcome` on transition.

fields.title: Refuse deprecated 'task start' instead of running claim
fields.description: Refuse the deprecated task start alias by printing its note and exiting non-zero, instead of going on to run task claim.
fields.context: Per E-1234, the alias prints a yellow deprecation note and then proceeds to call claim_item — soft deprecation.
fields.analysis:
Rationale: soft deprecation lets agents keep using the old verb; hard refusal forces them to learn 'task claim'.

The existing exit-with-ClickException pattern fits cleanly.

Reverts the call to claim_item in task_start_deprecated; keeps the hidden=True so the verb stays out of --help.

fields.title: Let task claim from a shell bind the sibling Claude session
fields.description: Let task claim run from a plain shell pane bind the task to the single live Claude session in the same tmux window, refusing when there is none or more than one.
fields.context:
Today, 'task claim' from a CLI shell only flips task status via the event path; the session→task binding only happens via the PreToolUse hook (which fires for Claude bash calls).

Per E-1205 user report.
fields.analysis:
Fix: when claim_item runs and current session does NOT resolve, scan tmux window for live Claude companions (via _read_live_companions + tmux list-panes).

If exactly 1 sibling Claude session: bind via a new 'task.claimed' event handled by Go executor.

If 0: refuse (claim is meaningless without a session) UNLESS --force (manual-work-without-Claude escape).

If 2+: refuse with message pointing at follow-up design ticket.

The hook path remains as fallback; this just makes the CLI usable from sibling panes.

fields.title: Fix 'task release' for missing, stale or competing bindings
fields.description: Fix endless task release so it releases a named task even when no current session can be resolved, and handles missing, stale or competing bindings.
fields.context:
Today release_item REQUIRES resolving the current Endless session id, then verifies ownership against it.

Per E-1205 user report.
fields.analysis:
Fix: split into two modes.

(1) Bare 'release' (no ID): resolve current session, fail with pointer to explicit-ID form if can't.

(2) 'release E-NNN': look up which session has E-NNN bound.

If none: error UNLESS --ignore-missing then info.

If a different LIVE session has it: refuse, name the live session.

If a DEAD/stale session has it (no live companion): clear the binding, report what happened.

fields.title: Design 'task claim' with several Claude sessions in a window
fields.description: Design how task claim from a shell pane picks which Claude session to bind when the tmux window has several, deciding which cases resolve automatically and which ask the user.
fields.context:
When 'task claim' runs from a non-Claude shell pane and the tmux window contains 2+ live Claude session companions, the binding target is ambiguous.

The first-pass implementation refuses with a 'specify which session' message.
fields.analysis:
Output: a plan file proposing rules with examples.

Implementation comes after the design lands.

fields.title: Fix status-row pane fallback to use the focused window
fields.description: Fix the Endless status row to show the focused tmux window's task when switching windows, instead of the most recently active task across the whole tmux session.
fields.context: `GetActiveTaskForPane` falls back from pane-specific to session-scoped lookup when the focused pane has no Endless session — so with multiple Claude sessions in different windows, every window resolves to the most-recently-active task across the whole tmux session.
fields.analysis: Fix: narrow the fallback to window-scoped (`tmux list-panes -t <pane>` without `-s`), so only panes in the focused window are considered.

fields.description: Improve the tmux popup menus with the task ID in the title, clearer labels and a centered hotkey popup, and add type, phase and tier to the status line.

fields.description: Fix the right-click menu to anchor at the mouse cursor on the status bar again instead of opening at the top-left of the screen.
fields.context: Regression from E-1246: changed the mouse-position bindings from `-x M -y S` (mouse X, status-line Y) to `-x M -y M` (mouse X and Y).

fields.title: Rename three task statuses and add an unapproved state
fields.description: Rename three task statuses to unplanned, underway and unverified, and add a new unapproved status.

fields.title: Fix right-click menu to anchor at the mouse cursor
fields.description: Fix the right-click menu so it reliably anchors at the mouse cursor instead of falling back to the top-left of the screen.
fields.notes: Deeper fix for the right-click menu position bug that E-1251 only superficially addressed.
fields.context: With E-1246`s refactor, bindings do `run-shell endless-tmux show-menu --position=mouse`, and my Go binary then invokes `tmux display-menu -x M -y S`.
fields.analysis:
Fix: capture `#{mouse_x}` and `#{mouse_y}` at binding time (tmux substitutes them while it still has the mouse event) and pass as numeric `--mouse-x` / `--mouse-y` flags to show-menu, which forwards them as `display-menu -x <num> -y <num>`.

Bindings need double-quoted run-shell args so tmux substitutes `#{...}`.

fields.description: Fix task claim's output to recommend the shipped esu shell helper instead of an eswt helper that shell-init does not provide.
fields.notes: If E-1180 later ships eswt for pure-cd, task claim output can stay on esu (the default we want most agents to use post-claim) or get a third branch — that's a design call for E-1180's plan.
fields.context:
task_cmd.py probes for an 'eswt' shell function and recommends running 'eval "$(endless shell-init)"' with the comment 'Adds eswt shell helper func'.

But shell-init does not currently ship eswt; it ships esu/esp/esf.

The recommendation is therefore misleading until E-1180 lands.

fields.title: Fix right-click menu vertical anchoring at the status line
fields.description: Fix the right-click menu's vertical position so it stays next to the status line where it was clicked instead of flipping to the top of the screen.
fields.notes: Follow-up to E-1253:
fields.context: tmux interprets `-y <mouse_y>` as "place menu top at this row"; when the click is near the bottom (status bar), the menu cannot extend below, and tmux auto-flips to the top rather than shifting up.
fields.analysis:
Fix: use `-y S` (line adjacent to status bar) regardless of the click Y.

The X stays as the captured numeric mouse_x.

Effectively this restores E-1236`s `-x M -y S` behavior with M correctly captured at binding time.

fields.title: Add a task bind command that leaves status unchanged
fields.description: Add endless task bind to attach the current session to a task for status-bar display, without changing the task's status or creating a worktree.
fields.context:
Use case: a task is `assumed` or `confirmed` and the user wants the bar to keep showing it as context.

fields.title: Detect already-landed tasks in worktree land
fields.description: Detect when worktree land runs after the task's worktree is gone and report that the task already landed, with its commit, instead of implying the work is lost.
fields.context:
It isn't; the branch is in main.

The worktree is NOT removed by landing: land leaves the directory and branch in place, and the reaper later removes BOTH (`git worktree remove` + `git branch -D`) once the task's task_landings row is older than worktree_ttl (default 14 days), or a human removed it manually (`git worktree remove` / `endless worktree drop`).

So a gone worktree is a later condition, not an immediate-after-land one — an immediate multi-session re-land still finds the worktree present and re-lands idempotently.
fields.analysis:
Scope decision (with Mike, 2026-07-11): FULL — A1 + A2 + B, unified by one new
`session-query last-landing` Go query. A1 (branch merged) is git-only; A2 (branch
also reaped) and B (rewrite/descendant gate) both need the landing SHA, so they
share the query. B was weighed against E-1417's in-flight after-conflict diagnosis:
kept because it upgrades the amend case from a guessed candidate (after a confusing
conflict) to a precise refusal BEFORE the rebase. E-1417 stays the safety net for
source conflicts B can't predetermine. E-1417 has LANDED (main @ b1efcc28), so E-1308
branches from current main and reuses E-1417's shipped recovery wording (no
rebase-onto-in-flight).

Recovery framing (Mike, 2026-07-11): Facet B's refusal must NOT prescribe a BARE
`git reset --hard` — whoever runs `land` may not be the branch's author, so a blanket
destructive command risks losing commits. Resolved by reusing E-1417's SHIPPED
already-landed recovery (verified in main @ b1efcc28): it captures the branch delta to
a patch BEFORE the reset, so no work is lost even if followed blindly. B extracts that
block into a shared `_already_landed_recovery(wt, base)` and adds an ownership-confirm
note. (Earlier worry that E-1417 prescribed a bare reset was wrong — it already
candidate-frames with a "can duplicate or lose work" caveat and captures the delta
first.)

---

Added case (Claude session, 2026-07-09; now folded into the plan as Facet B):

The `git branch --merged main` test catches only FULLY-merged branches. It misses
the re-land failure where a branch's commit was `git commit --amend`-ed AFTER its
content had already been landed: the branch is a partial duplicate of main plus a
new delta — not fully merged — so `--merged` is false and land proceeds into a
source-file rebase conflict.

Gate (reuses task_landings, which records each landing's SHA): on a re-land (task
has >=1 task_landings row), require the branch HEAD to be a descendant of the last
landed SHA — `git merge-base --is-ancestor <last_landed_sha> HEAD`. A correct
follow-up (a new commit stacked on a branch first rebased onto main) passes; an
amend/rewrite fails. On failure, refuse BEFORE the rebase and print the reset+reapply
recovery rather than a misleading auto-file message.

Concrete repro: E-1750's first commit was landed; a follow-up was made by amending
that commit instead of stacking a new one; the next `just land` rebase re-applied the
whole change onto a main that already had it -> CONFLICT in
internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go. Recovery was manual reset-to-main +
re-apply-delta. Couples to E-1417 (the diagnosis half).

## From the description

via `git branch --merged main` when the branch survives, or the recorded landing when the branch was reaped too.

Fall back to today's error only when the work is genuinely unaccounted for.

fields.title: Set skip-worktree on Claude settings in sandbox bind
fields.description: Set skip-worktree on the worktree's .claude/settings.json after sandbox bind writes to it, so the modified file no longer blocks rebase on land.
fields.context: The tracked-modified file blocks rebase during endless worktree land until manually fixed (hit during E-1342 land 2026-05-15, resolved with manual git update-index --skip-worktree).
fields.analysis:
## Reopened 2026-08-20 — the fix inverted the failure mode rather than removing it

E-1347 shipped `git update-index --skip-worktree .claude/settings.json` because
the *tracked-modified* file blocked rebase during `worktree land` (hit landing
E-1342). That remedy trades one rebase blocker for the opposite one: skip-worktree
tells git the file must not be touched, so git now refuses to check out any
commit that CHANGES it.

Same command, same file, same land step, mirrored trigger:

| | before E-1347 | after E-1347 |
|---|---|---|
| blocked when | the worktree modified the file | **main** modifies the file |
| git says | local changes would be overwritten | local changes would be overwritten |
| how often | every worktree with a sandbox bind | every live worktree, simultaneously |

The second row is worse in blast radius. The pre-E-1347 failure was per-worktree
and self-inflicted; this one fires in *every* self-dev worktree alive at the
moment a commit touching `.claude/settings.json` lands on main, and the developer
who is blocked never edited that file.

## Evidence — the E-1997 land (folded from E-1998)

`just land` for E-1997 failed with:

```
Error: rebase conflict while rebasing your branch onto main.

Conflicting files:
  (none reported)
```

The empty file list is the tell. The real git failure was upstream of any
conflict:

```
error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by checkout:
	.claude/settings.json
Please commit your changes or stash them before you switch branches.
Aborting
error: could not detach HEAD
```

`git ls-files -v .claude/settings.json` in the worktree reported `S`
(skip-worktree). Main had advanced with commit `029208d9`, adding
`"autoMemoryEnabled": false` to the tracked `.claude/settings.json`. No commit on
the branch was involved; the rebase never started.

Manual recovery that worked:

```sh
git update-index --no-skip-worktree .claude/settings.json
git checkout -- .claude/settings.json
git rebase main
```

Deliberately NOT followed by `just claude-settings-init`, since regenerating the
file re-arms the collision for the next land.

## Design tension to resolve (not a decision)

E-998 wants the regenerated per-worktree override invisible to `git status`;
landing wants the file checkout-able. skip-worktree buys the first at the cost of
the second, and E-1347 is where that trade was made. Options worth weighing:

- Clear skip-worktree for the duration of the rebase inside `worktree land` and
  restore it after. Narrow; preserves E-998's contract; fixes only the land path.
- Stop tracking a per-worktree `.claude/settings.json` at all — leave the
  committed file alone and put the override somewhere git does not track. Removes
  the tension instead of timing around it.
- `--assume-unchanged` instead of `--skip-worktree`. Different semantics; verify
  whether git also refuses the checkout before assuming it helps.

## Scope

self_dev only. `claude-settings-init` refuses to run from the main checkout and
is not part of a downstream project's worktree bootstrap, so a project that
merely *uses* endless never sets the bit and never sees this.

## Related, deliberately not merged here

The misleading "rebase conflict / (none reported)" wrapper and its `reset --hard`
recovery suggestion belong to E-1957 (and E-1272 for the destructive hint). Those
mislabel *any* non-conflict rebase failure; fixing this task removes one trigger,
not the misclassification.

## The unnamed option above has a name: `.claude/settings.local.json` (2026-09-08, with Mike)

The second option — "put the override somewhere git does not track" — is not
hypothetical machinery. Claude Code already provides the file for it, and this
repo already gitignores it (the `settings.local.json` rule in `.gitignore`,
which the comment block there says is "exclusively Claude's local-settings
file"). It sits at Local tier, ABOVE project settings in precedence, and
Claude Code merges it natively.

Writing the generated per-worktree override there instead of overwriting the
tracked `.claude/settings.json` removes the collision outright rather than
timing around it: nothing is tracked, so nothing needs skip-worktree, so no
rebase can ever be refused over it. The committed `settings.json` stays exactly
as it is, carrying `enabledPlugins` for everyone, and main can change it freely.

### E-998's two reasons for rejecting it do not hold

Mike concurred with this assessment on 2026-09-08.

1. *"Single owner per file"* — the claim was that `settings.local.json` is
   hand-edited by the user for `permissions`, so writing there would force a
   read-merge-write. But `claude-settings-init` ALREADY does a read-merge-write
   on `settings.json` — that is exactly how it preserves `enabledPlugins` while
   replacing the hooks block. The complexity is identical and already paid; it
   would just be paid against a different file.

2. *"Moving the override to settings.local.json would not stop the user-level
   hook from firing"* — true, and irrelevant here. That addresses E-998's
   hook-DUPLICATION goal. It is not an argument that the file fails at the
   tracking problem, which is what this task is about. Two different problems
   were answered with one rejection.

### Why this is not the sandbox

The generated override must sit where Claude Code discovers settings — the
project root's `.claude/`. Claude Code will not read it from a sandbox
directory, so relocating it there cannot work without a symlink. That makes
this file NOT an instance of the "test-time files belong in the sandbox"
principle (E-2035/E-2050); it is its own, simpler fix. Keeping the two separate
matters, because folding this in as a sandbox case would attach the wrong
remedy to it.

### Measured cost of leaving it alone

2026-09-08: 128 of 132 worktrees on this machine carry the skip-worktree bit on
`.claude/settings.json`. A single main-checkout commit touching that file
blocks the rebase in every one of them simultaneously, each reporting a failure
that names no conflicting file. It has now happened at least three times
(landing E-1997, landing E-2107's follow-up E-2122, and the E-1733 worktree).

### Verify before implementing

Confirm empirically that Claude Code merges `settings.local.json` over
`settings.json` for the `hooks` and `env` keys specifically — E-998's plan
asserted merge semantics without testing them, and this task should not repeat
that. A throwaway project with both files and a trivial hook settles it.

## From the description

Fix: have sandbox bind run git update-index --skip-worktree on the file after writing, matching the claude-settings-init contract.

fields.title: Consolidate the Go binaries into one endless-go binary
fields.description: Consolidate the six separate endless-* Go binaries into a single endless-go binary that exposes them as subcommands, leaving one install target and one symlink.
fields.context: Today we ship endless-event, endless-hook, endless-channel, endless-sandbox, endless-serve, endless-tmux as separate Go binaries — six install targets, six symlinks to refresh on every just-install, six entries to wrap in bin-sandbox/, six lookups when subprocesses spawn.
fields.analysis:
One install target, one symlink, one wrapper if any sandbox routing is still needed.

Reduces the proliferation surface Mike has flagged repeatedly.

fields.title: Replace sandbox wrapper scripts with sandbox self-detection
fields.description: Replace the bin-sandbox wrapper scripts with each Go binary detecting at startup that it runs in a worktree sandbox and using that sandbox's config.
fields.analysis:
Each endless-* binary on startup walks up from cwd looking for an endless-managed worktree (e.g. .endless/worktree.json marker) and the corresponding ~/.cache/endless/sandboxes/worktree-e-NNN/ — if both present, self-set ConfigDir to that path before any consumer reads it.

This eliminates the two-layer architecture (wrappers + binaries) that caused the bin-sandbox/endless-event-execs-stale-global-binary bug observed during E-1322 verification.

Reuses the existing monitor.IsSandboxActive() pattern, reversed: instead of detecting whether a caller routed us into sandbox, the binary routes itself.

Removes one hyphenated dir; no PATH manipulation needed; works identically for shell-invoked and hook-fired calls.

fields.title: Refuse --force on task claim when run by Claude
fields.description: Refuse --force on task claim and similar commands when run by Claude Code, pointing instead to the legitimate command for the situation.
fields.context: --force on 'endless task claim' is documented as 'manual work, no Claude assistance' — but Claude reads the error and reaches for --force anyway, because the error text presents it as the next step.
fields.analysis:
Gate, not guardrail: removes the bypass entirely from Claude's reach.

Generalize to any --force flag in any endless verb where the legitimate case doesn't apply to a Claude session.

fields.title: Add a command to rebind an orphaned session
fields.description: Add endless session rebind to recover a live Claude session that lost its companion file: regenerate the file, revive its sessions row and bind it to the task.
fields.context:
When a Claude session loses its companion file (e.g. via the worktree-delete-on-land cascade addressed by E-1337) but the Claude process is still alive, today there is no legitimate verb to recover.

claim --force disclaims the session entirely; task bind has the same missing-companion precondition as claim.
fields.analysis:
Obsoleted 2026-09-20. The verb's entire mechanism was 'regenerates the companion file from current TMUX_PANE + CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID'. Session companion files no longer exist — the `.endless/sessions/` path was pruned, and register.py's gitignore comment records that new projects must never scaffold it. A verb defined as repairing a file that cannot be missing because it is never written has no remaining premise.

Never shipped (status was `submitted`), so obsolete is legal here rather than the `replaced_by` relation the guide requires for work that already landed.

NOT obsolete because something else covers it: the recovery need it was filed for — a live session whose window identity is wrong — is real and is now the subject of the tmux-crash recovery discussion on E-1983. What died is this task's mechanism, not the problem class.

## From the description

Bypasses the precondition by fixing its upstream cause (missing companion), not by skipping the check.

Refuses when CLAUDECODE is not set or TMUX_PANE is unset — the verb's premise is 'recover an alive Claude session'.

fields.title: Add session bind as an alias for task bind
fields.description: Add endless session bind as an alias for endless task bind, for users thinking of the binding from the session side, with no behavior change.
fields.notes: for the orphaned-session case see E-1370.
fields.context:
endless task bind exists and is correctly task-centric, matching the project's verb convention.

But the natural mental model when the user (or Claude) is thinking 'this SESSION needs to be associated with a task' is session-centric.
fields.analysis:
No behavior change; just findability for the session-centric framing.

Same precondition (companion file must exist);

fields.title: Reap snapshots of declined and obsolete tasks
fields.description: Reap plan snapshots of tasks that end declined or obsolete without landing, and decide whether pending snapshots never claimed by a task are in scope.
fields.context: Snapshots under .git/info/endless/snapshots/e-NNN/ remain after the task's lifecycle ends without land (status declined or obsolete).
fields.analysis:
Trigger TBD — e.g. on task status flip to declined/obsolete, or a scheduled prune, or both.

Related concern: pending snapshots whose session never claims a task also accumulate; in scope or follow-up TBD.

fields.title: Stop auto-creating worktrees for decisions on task update
fields.description: Stop task update --text from creating a worktree for decisions, writing the plan file directly into the main checkout instead.
fields.context:
Decisions are record-type items — their deliverable is the description + attached plan file, not implementation work.

Observed 2026-05-16 when attaching the plan file to E-1373: created worktree-e-1373 and its sandbox solely to hold a plan file commit.
fields.analysis: Gate: when row.type='decision', skip the worktree-creation branch; write the plan file directly into the project's main checkout under .endless/plans/.

fields.title: Refuse task confirm and task assume for decisions
fields.description: Refuse task confirm and task assume for decisions and direct the user to task complete instead.
fields.context:
task_cmd.py docstring already establishes the convention: 'task confirm / task assume' for implementation tasks (behavior to verify), 'task complete' for findings-as-deliverable tasks.

A decision is the outcome-as-deliverable shape: the description + attached plan file IS the deliverable.

Observed 2026-05-16: E-1373 (type=decision) was marked confirmed during worktree land — should have been completed.
fields.analysis:
There's nothing to verify behaviorally.

Consider whether decisions need a pre-complete state at all, or whether 'ready' -> 'completed' is sufficient.

fields.title: Show the outcome after the description in task show
fields.description: Show the outcome after the description in task show, with its label on its own line instead of a colon-suffixed label.

fields.title: Move decisions into their own table
fields.description: Move decisions out of the tasks table into their own table with a decision-shaped schema and a proposed, accepted or rejected lifecycle, with no phase, worktree or verify state.
fields.context:
Decisions are currently stored as tasks rows with type='decision'.

Sharing the table with implementation tasks means task-only operations (worktree auto-create, task confirm/assume, status flow assuming verify-before-confirmed) get applied to decisions where they don't make sense - observed 2026-05-16 with E-1373 (worktree created just to hold a plan file; 'confirmed' used where 'complete' was correct), prompting band-aid gates E-1375/E-1376.
fields.analysis:
ED-NNN local-ID convention per E-1031/E-1032/E-1261.

A new decision_relations table holds decision-sourced edges; task-sourced edges (including task->decision) stay in task_deps until E-1389 renames it.

The 'endless decision ...' CLI surface stays stable; only storage changes.

fields.title: Fix session-touch capture skipping every task event

fields.analysis:
Fix: in internal/events/session_tasks.go, change shouldRecordSessionTouch to 'return evt.Actor.SessionID != ""' (drop the ActorKind check).

Update the test that asserts CLI-actor produces no row — it asserted the buggy behavior.

fields.title: Add a surrogate id primary key to session_tasks

Mike's 35+ years of DB experience: all tables get an id field, full stop.

fields.title: Fail loudly in hooks when session setup is missing

fields.title: Allow task spawn from the session claiming the task

Discovered 2026-05-16 during E-1378 implementation prep when the design session needed to hand off to a fresh implementation session.

Fix in task_cmd.py spawn_plan: when the spawning session's id equals the current claimant's id, auto-release before pre-claim, then proceed with normal spawn flow (SessionStart's @endless_spawned_by hook binds the new session).

Keep the refusal in place when the current claimant is a DIFFERENT live session — that's a real conflict.

fields.title: Refuse to emit events without a resolvable session
fields.description: Refuse to emit an event, with an actionable error, when its session can't be determined, instead of silently dropping the session and losing attribution.
fields.notes: Pair with E-1402 (resolver strengthening) so the error fires only when truly impossible.
fields.context:
Downstream: session_tasks (and every future per-kind table) loses attribution.

6 rows had to be backfilled manually for tasks E-1390-E-1396 today; that's not sustainable.

Mike: 'Inability to determine a valid session ID and to do so accurately and robustness should be treated as a FIVE ALARM FIRE.'
fields.analysis: Fix: emit_event MUST refuse to emit when session_id cannot be resolved deterministically — error with actionable message (run endless task bind <id>) rather than silently degrading.

fields.title: Strengthen the session resolver for multiple Claude panes
fields.description: Strengthen the session resolver to return a session whenever a defensible choice exists among several Claude panes, using a deterministic precedence rule.
fields.notes: Pairs with E-1401 — both required for the FIVE-ALARM fix to be complete.
fields.context:
E-1294's single-sibling fallback resolves _current_endless_session_id only when EXACTLY one other Claude pane is alive.

With 5+ active sessions today, the fallback refused to resolve, leaving emit_event with no session_id.
fields.analysis:

the gate (E-1401) only fires when no defensible choice is possible.

fields.title: Refuse unattributed event writes inside Claude

fields.title: Migrate all primary keys to AUTOINCREMENT
fields.description: Migrate every table's integer primary key to AUTOINCREMENT so SQLite never reuses the IDs of deleted rows, which breaks cross-references that outlive a delete.
fields.context:
All tables currently declare 'id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY' (without AUTOINCREMENT).

SQLite reuses deleted IDs in this mode —

confirmed 2026-05-17 when E-1403 was reused for a new task immediately after the prior E-1403 was deleted.

ID reuse breaks any cross-reference that survives a delete (outcome text, ledger entries, decisions, plan files).
fields.analysis:
Migration: drop+recreate each table preserving data, change column to 'id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT', seed sqlite_sequence with the current max(id).

Tables to audit: tasks, sessions, projects, focuses, channels, conversations, messages, notes, task_deps, task_files, session_messages, session_tasks, session_statuses, session_gates, suggestions, activity.

E-1344 (soft delete) addresses the same concern via a different lever; both belong long-term — AUTOINCREMENT is belt-and-suspenders for any future hard-purge path.
